C0.quote: we introduce a new voting formalism to support long-term collective decision making
C0.note: Voting rules aggregating approval ballots over repeated decisions.

C1.quote: axiomatic analysis as well as a quantitative evaluation by computer simulations
C1.note: OT: introduction of the perpetual voting formalism and new rules/metrics.

C2.1.quote: perpetual voting formalism based on approval ballots

C2.2.quote: each voter v ∈ N approves some non-empty subset of C

C2.3.quote: Three of them prefer French food, two of them Indian food
C2.3.note: Also 'preferences in A_{k+1}' and 'misrepresent their preferences' in Section 7.

C2.4.quote: beneficial for voters to misrepresent their preferences (or abstain)
C2.4.note: Formal model treats approval profile as the preferences (would be IDU), but Section 7 says submitted may differ from held; DIST listed first, so chosen.

C3.1.note: Strategic behaviour only discussed informally as future work (freerider effect); no analysis.

C3.2.note: No statement that voters report truthfully.

C4.1.loc: Section 2 Definition 1, p.2104; Section 3 Perpetual Nash; Section 6
C4.1.quote: the satisfaction of a voter is the number of past decisions
C4.1.note: Satisfaction defined by approval of winner; Nash utility defined as satisfaction; simulation generates approvals from distances in a Euclidean model.

C5.1.quote: enable minorities to have a fair (proportional) influence on the decision process

C5.2.quote: voters receive at least a “fair share” of favorable choices
C5.2.note: Satisfaction, quota, influence defined on approval profile; no statement relating it to held attitudes.

VOT.quote_behav: each voter v ∈ N approves some non-empty subset of C
VOT.note: Voters' approvals are exogenous inputs in all analyses; strategic behaviour only mentioned in Section 7 as open issue.

C8.1.note: NA: no type is STRAT or MIXED.

claims.quote: We identify two perpetual voting rules as particularly recommendable in long-term collective decision making
perpetual voting rules can be beneficial in all repeated collective decision making scenarios
we obtain a sustainable (stable) process of collective decision making

C9.2.note: Recommendation of rules for real settings needs: approvals reflect voters' held preferences / sincere reporting (not stated; Section 7 notes freerider misreporting), approvals as satisfaction (stated), agents' info/behaviour (unstated).
